newsitem.title: USA: Mass Gov's school budget would cut repairs - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mass Gov's school budget would cut repairs - paper.

text.p: Massachusetts Gov. William Weld's new budget, if approved, would force nearly 50 public schools that had planned on repairs to wait another year, the Boston Globe reported Wednesday.
The governor proposed spending $17.1 million on school construction for 1999 fiscal year -- a nearly 50 percent cut from the $32.9 million budget proposed for fiscal 1998.

The cuts mean that only 24 of the 132 schools on a state waiting list would be renovated, the paper said. It added the budget put forward by the state Department of Education would pay for repairs at 49 schools.
Senate President Thomas Birmingham told the Globe that Weld's school construction budget was surprising, given the governor had made a pro-education State of the State address in January.
The paper said the legislature likely will restore the funds cut by the governor.
